title: Improving Long-Context Retrieval with Multi-Prefix Embedding
abstract: Long-context retrieval exposes a tension: single-vector embeddings lose fine-grained detail, while token-level multi-vector methods incur prohibitive storage. We propose Multi-Prefix Embedding (MPE), which partitions a document into chunks separated by EOS tokens, encodes the full sequence in a single causal forward pass, and extracts one embedding at each prefix boundary. MPE retains cross-chunk context, enables chunk-level MaxSim matching, and trains with only document-level relevance labels. Experiments on MLDR-en, BrowseComp-Plus, and LongEmbed show that MPE is competitive with or outperforms single-vector, independent-chunk, and multi-vector baselines, while providing a natural source attribution mechanism for locating evidence chunks.

significance.justification: The paper introduces MPE which provides measurable gains in long-context retrieval performance while maintaining practical storage efficiency, directly impacting how builders approach RAG architecture decisions.

novelty.justification: MPE represents a substantial new variation that combines single-pass encoding with multi-vector extraction at prefix boundaries, distinct from prior single-vector and independent-chunk approaches.

reproducibility.justification: The method is clearly described with partitioning strategy and extraction process specified, but no mention of code or artifacts being publicly available.

clarity.justification: The paper is well-written with clear problem framing, method description, and evaluation across multiple benchmarks with appropriate scope of claims.

topical_fit.justification: Directly addresses core LLM builder concerns with retrieval-augmented generation and long-context processing, squarely in the applied-AI sweet spot.
